terms.definition: A muscular pump about the size of your fist that squeezes to push blood through your body.
terms.function: Beats continuously, pushing blood out through arteries and receiving returning blood through veins, driving both the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
terms.whereItIs: Center of the chest, slightly left of the body's midline, between the lungs.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the engine of the entire circulation process — without its continuous pumping, no blood would move and no cell would get oxygen or nutrients.
terms.relatedConcept: Arteries carry blood away from heart

terms.conceptId: Arteries carry blood away from heart
terms.definition: A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart, usually carrying oxygen-rich blood.
terms.function: Carries blood away from the heart under high pressure through thick, muscular, elastic walls, branching into smaller arterioles as it nears tissues.
terms.whereItIs: Starting at the aortic arch just above the heart and branching outward through the neck, arms, abdomen, and legs.
terms.whyItMatters: Arteries are the high-pressure delivery lines of the body — their direction (away from the heart), not their oxygen content, is what defines them.

terms.definition: A blood vessel that carries blood back toward the heart, usually carrying oxygen-poor blood.
terms.function: Carries blood back toward the heart at lower pressure through thinner walls; many contain one-way valves that keep blood moving in a single direction against gravity.
terms.whereItIs: Converging on the superior and inferior vena cava, which empty into the heart's right atrium.
terms.whyItMatters: Veins complete the loop — without them, blood delivered by the arteries would have no way back to the heart to be sent out again.
terms.relatedConcept: Arteries carry blood away from heart

terms.definition: A tiny, thin-walled blood vessel where oxygen, nutrients, and waste move between blood and body cells.
terms.function: Connects the smallest arteries to the smallest veins; walls are thin enough (often one cell thick) that gases and nutrients pass directly through them into and out of tissue.
terms.whereItIs: Fine mesh networks at the body's periphery and inside organs, where artery and vein branches visibly dissolve into a web of hair-thin vessels.
terms.whyItMatters: Capillaries are the actual delivery point of the whole circulatory system — every other vessel exists just to get blood to and from these exchange sites.
terms.relatedConcept: Arteries carry blood away from heart

terms.definition: The short loop of blood flow between the heart and the lungs, where blood picks up oxygen and drops off carbon dioxide.
terms.function: The right side of the heart sends oxygen-poor blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen and release carbon dioxide, then the refreshed blood returns to the heart's left side.
terms.whereItIs: Just lateral to the heart, at lung height — a short, direct loop compared to the systemic circuit.
terms.whyItMatters: This is the one exception to the artery/vein oxygen rule: the pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood toward the lungs, and the pulmonary vein carries oxygen-rich blood back to the heart — the reverse of every other artery and vein in the body.

terms.definition: The long loop of blood flow between the heart and the rest of the body, delivering oxygen and picking up waste.
terms.function: The left side of the heart sends oxygen-rich blood out to every organ and tissue, and oxygen-poor blood returns through the veins to the heart's right side.
terms.whereItIs: Runs the length of the body — from the descending aorta through the abdomen and out to the limbs and organs.
terms.whyItMatters: This is the loop that actually delivers oxygen and nutrients to every living cell in the body, making it the reason circulation exists at all.

terms.definition: One of the two upper chambers of the heart that receive incoming blood.
terms.function: Collects blood arriving from the veins (right atrium from the body, left atrium from the lungs) and passes it down into the matching ventricle.
terms.whereItIs: The top two chambers of the heart, above the ventricles.
terms.whyItMatters: Atria are why the heart can receive blood continuously while it's also pumping blood out — the two jobs happen in different chambers at the same time.

terms.definition: One of the two lower chambers of the heart that pump blood out to the lungs or body.
terms.function: Contracts forcefully to push blood out through an artery — the right ventricle to the lungs via the pulmonary artery, the left ventricle to the body via the aorta.
terms.whereItIs: The bottom two chambers of the heart, below the atria.
terms.whyItMatters: The ventricles generate the pressure that actually drives blood all the way around both circuits — the left ventricle in particular has the thickest, strongest muscle wall of any heart chamber because it pumps blood to the entire body.
